feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is claimed for it. The candidate is valid and consistent with the evidence. Its geometry is unchanged from iteration 3 (five 8 mm sensors at x = -0.016 to +0.016, y = 0.03, mass 0.7), so the change is confined to the controller: kp 2.0 to 3.0, kd 0.2 to 0.3, ki 0.8 to 0.4, base_speed 1.3 held. Iteration 3 (ki 0.8, base 1.3) is the best raced design at 68.36, and every iteration so far ended off_track with max_error at 0.061 to 0.064 and 1 to 2 line-loss events, so the constant overshoot past the 0.06 m limit is the problem to fix. Iteration 3 showed that ki changes alone moved the score only a little. Iteration 1 (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, ki 0.05, base 1.5) scored 65.9. This candidate raises kp, which the evidence has not yet isolated: iteration 0 used kp 3.0 but also had 12 mm sensors and mass 0.8, so its result (26.0) cannot be read as a clean kp effect. Two things to watch in the race. (1) If steering_oscillation rises well above the roughly 0.10 to 0.16 range seen so far while max_error stays near 0.06, kd 0.3 with kp 3.0 is too much damping-to-gain mismatch and kd should come back toward 0.2. (2) If the robot holds the line but progress stays low, speed is the limit and base_speed should rise from 1.3 toward 1.5. If max_error still sits at or above 0.06 with line-loss events, the sensor span is the next lever: widen the outer sensors (for example x to plus or minus 0.024 with 8 mm footprints, as in iteration 2, which did not help at y = 0.05) or shift the forward position, before changing gains further. Approving now gives telemetry on the kp effect, which earlier iterations could not isolate, and several iterations remain to act on it.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises clearly above the roughly 0.10 to 0.16 seen in iterations 0 to 3 while max_error stays near 0.06, lower kd from 0.3 toward 0.2, since iteration 1 showed kd 0.2 already raising jitter at kp 2.0.

If the robot holds the line (line_loss_events of 1 or fewer) but progress stays below about 0.3, raise base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.5, since iteration 1 at base 1.5 reached 0.16 to 0.21 progress and iteration 3 at base 1.3 was slower to finish.

If max_error stays at or above 0.06 with line-loss events of 1 or more, keep the gains and widen the sensor span (for example outer sensors at x of plus or minus 0.024 with 8 mm footprints, or a forward shift of the sensors), because the line is lost at bends regardless of kp, as iterations 0 to 3 show.
